blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 1 (Graphical Representation of Functions), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 Sketch the graph of \(y = -(x + 3)(x - 1)\) using the method of factors: find the x-intercepts, vertex, end behaviour and y-intercept. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: It is already in the form \(a(x - h)(x - k)\) with \(a = -1\), \(h = -3\), \(k = 1\); use the four steps of Case-I.

book_ref.quote: To sketch the graph, follow the given steps:

steps: End behaviour: \(a = -1 < 0\), so \(y \to -\infty\) as \(x \to \pm\infty\); the parabola opens downward
Symmetry about \(x = -1\): the mirror of \((0, 3)\) is \((-2, 3)\); check \(-(1)(-3) = 3\)

blocks.prompt: 2 Sketch the graph of \(y = 3x^{2} - 12x + 12\) after writing it in factor form. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Take out the common factor 3; the bracket is a perfect square, so Case-II (\(h = k\)) applies.

book_ref.quote: Then follow Steps 3 and 4 of Case-I to complete the sketch of the graph.

steps: The graph touches the x-axis only at \(x = 2\), so the vertex is \((2, 0)\)
Plot \((2, 0)\), \((0, 12)\), \((4, 12)\) and draw an upward parabola touching the x-axis at \((2, 0)\)
blocks.final_answer: \(y = 3(x - 2)^{2}\): upward parabola touching the x-axis at the vertex \((2, 0)\), through \((0, 12)\) and \((4, 12)\).

blocks.prompt: 3 A parabola cuts the x-axis at \(x = -4\) and \(x = 2\) and passes through \((1, -10)\). Find its equation in standard form and its vertex. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the factor form from the intercepts, then use the third point to find \(a\).

book_ref.quote: If the graph crosses the x-axis at

blocks.prompt: 4 Discuss the domain, range, intercepts, monotonicity and asymptote of \(f(x) = \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^{x}\), make a table for \(x = -2, \ldots, 2\) and describe its graph. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the properties of \(a^{x}\) with \(a = \frac{5}{2} > 1\), then a few values.

book_ref.quote: Before sketching the graph of an exponential function, we study its essential properties

steps: y-intercept \((0, 1)\); no x-intercept because \(\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^{x} = 0\) has no solution
Graph: a smooth rising curve through these points, above the x-axis, approaching it on the left

blocks.prompt: 5 Prove that \(f(x) = a^{x}\) is strictly increasing when \(a > 1\) and strictly decreasing when \(0 < a < 1\). Hence show that it is one-to-one. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write \(a^{x_{2}} = a^{x_{1}} \cdot a^{x_{2} - x_{1}}\) and compare the second factor with 1.

book_ref.quote: is strictly increasing when \(a > 1\)

steps: Injective: if \(a^{x_{1}} = a^{x_{2}}\) with \(x_{1} \ne x_{2}\), one would be strictly bigger by the two cases, which is impossible
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a^{x}\) is strictly increasing for \(a > 1\), strictly decreasing for \(0 < a < 1\), and one-to-one.

blocks.prompt: 6 Show that \(\cosh x + \sinh x = e^{x}\) and \(\cosh x - \sinh x = e^{-x}\). Hence prove \(\cosh^{2} x - \sinh^{2} x = 1\) and verify it for \(x = \ln 3\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Add and subtract the two definitions, then use the difference of squares.

book_ref.quote: The other four are made from them exactly as in trigonometry

steps: \(\cosh^{2} x - \sinh^{2} x = (\cosh x + \sinh x)(\cosh x - \sinh x) = e^{x} \cdot e^{-x} = e^{0} = 1\)

blocks.prompt: 7 Show that \(\tanh x = \dfrac{e^{2x} - 1}{e^{2x} + 1}\). Hence show that \(-1 < \tanh x < 1\) for every real \(x\), and find \(\tanh 1\) to four decimal places. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Multiply the numerator and denominator of the definition by \(e^{x}\); then compare the numerator with the denominator.

book_ref.quote: is always smaller in size than its denominator

blocks.prompt: 8 Prove that \(\cosh x \ge 1\) for every real \(x\), with equality only at \(x = 0\). Hence state the range of \(\cosh x\) and show that \(\cosh x\) is even. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: A square is never negative: start from \(\left(e^{x/2} - e^{-x/2}\right)^{2} \ge 0\).

book_ref.quote: is minimum value of the graph

steps: \(\cosh x = \frac{e^{x} + e^{-x}}{2} \ge 1\); equality when \(e^{x/2} = e^{-x/2}\), i.e. \(x = 0\)
As \(x \to \pm\infty\), one of \(e^{x}\), \(e^{-x}\) tends to \(\infty\), so \(\cosh x \to \infty\); being continuous, the range is \([1, \infty)\)
\(\cosh(-x) = \frac{e^{-x} + e^{x}}{2} = \cosh x\): even, symmetric about the y-axis
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\cosh x \ge 1\) (minimum 1 at \(x = 0\)), range \([1, \infty)\), and \(\cosh x\) is even.

blocks.prompt: 9 Prove that \(\sinh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right)\) for every real \(x\). Use it to find \(y\) if \(\sinh y = \frac{12}{5}\), and check your answer. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Put \(x = \sinh y\), get a quadratic in \(e^{y}\), reject the negative root, take \(\ln\).

book_ref.quote: it is clear from the horizontal line test that the function is bijective

steps: Let \(y = \sinh^{-1} x\); then \(x = \sinh y = \frac{e^{y} - e^{-y}}{2}\), so \(2xe^{y} = e^{2y} - 1\)

blocks.prompt: 10 Prove that \(\cosh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\right)\), \(x \ge 1\). Evaluate \(\cosh^{-1}\frac{5}{3}\) and show what the rejected sign would give. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Same method as for \(\sinh^{-1}\); now both roots are positive, and the condition \(y \ge 0\) chooses the sign.

book_ref.quote: which is possible only if the positive sign is taken

steps: Since \(y \ge 0\), take the plus sign: \(\cosh^{-1} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\right)\) (at \(x = 1\) both give 0)
The minus sign gives \(\ln\left(\frac{5}{3} - \frac{4}{3}\right) = \ln\frac{1}{3} = -\ln 3 < 0\), not allowed

blocks.prompt: 11 Prove that \(f(x) = \log_{a} x\) (\(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\)) is one-to-one, strictly increasing for \(a > 1\) and strictly decreasing for \(0 < a < 1\). Illustrate with \(\log_{2}\) and \(\log_{1/2}\) at \(x = 2\) and \(x = 8\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Change to exponential form \(x = a^{y}\) and use what is known about \(a^{y}\).

book_ref.quote: Hence, the logarithmic function is one to one.

steps: One-to-one: \(\log_{a} s = \log_{a} t \Rightarrow a^{\log_{a} s} = a^{\log_{a} t} \Rightarrow s = t\) (using \(a^{\log_{a} x} = x\))
If \(a > 1\), \(a^{y}\) is increasing, so \(a^{y_{1}} < a^{y_{2}} \Rightarrow y_{1} < y_{2}\): \(\log_{a} x\) strictly increasing
If \(0 < a < 1\), \(a^{y}\) is decreasing, so \(a^{y_{1}} < a^{y_{2}} \Rightarrow y_{1} > y_{2}\): strictly decreasing
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\log_{a} x\) is one-to-one, strictly increasing for \(a > 1\) and strictly decreasing for \(0 < a < 1\).

blocks.prompt: 12 Let \(f(x) = 3^{x - 1} + 2\). Find \(f^{-1}(x)\), state the domain and range of \(f\) and \(f^{-1}\), and verify with one point that the graphs are reflections in \(y = x\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(f\) is one-to-one (an increasing exponential, shifted); interchange \(x\) and \(y\) and solve for \(y\).

book_ref.quote: The graph of a function and its inverse are related through a geometric symmetry

steps: \(3^{x - 1} > 0\), so \(f(x) > 2\): domain of \(f\) is \(\mathbb{R}\), range \(]2, \infty[\); \(3^{x}\) is strictly increasing, so \(f\) is one-to-one
Domain of \(f^{-1}\) is \(]2, \infty[\) (range of \(f\)); range of \(f^{-1}\) is \(\mathbb{R}\) (domain of \(f\))

blocks.prompt: 13 Let \(f(x) = 2^{x}\). Find the function obtained by applying in order: a shift 3 units to the left, a vertical stretch by factor 4 and a shift 2 units downward. Find the new y-intercept and horizontal asymptote. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Apply one transformation at a time to the newest function.

book_ref.quote: Never go back to the original function in the middle.

blocks.prompt: 14 Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 1}\). Find the function obtained by applying in order: a horizontal compression by factor 2, a shift 1 unit to the right, a vertical compression by factor 3 and a shift 2 units upward. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Name each new function and replace every \(x\) for a horizontal change; work on the whole function for a vertical change.

book_ref.quote: Write the function you have now and give it a name.

steps: Check: the vertical asymptote \(x = 1\) goes to \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) then \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), matching \(6x - 9 = 0\)

blocks.prompt: 15 Solve the equation \(4^{x} - 6 \cdot 2^{x} + 8 = 0\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(4^{x} = (2^{x})^{2}\), so the equation is a quadratic in \(t = 2^{x} > 0\); then use the one-to-one property.

book_ref.quote: Ordinary algebra cannot reach it there

blocks.prompt: 16 Solve \(\log_{2} x + \log_{2}(x - 2) = 3\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Domain first, then the product law, exponential form, and reject roots outside the domain.

book_ref.quote: Several logarithms: join them with the product or quotient law

blocks.prompt: 17 Solve \(\log_{x}(4x - 3) = 2\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the base and argument conditions, change to exponential form, solve, then test each root.

book_ref.quote: here the unknown is also the base

steps: \(x = 1\) is not allowed as a base: rejected

blocks.prompt: 18 Solve \(5^{x} = 2^{x + 2}\). Give the exact answer as one logarithm and to four decimal places. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The bases cannot be made equal, so take \(\ln\) of both sides; the equation becomes linear in \(x\).

book_ref.quote: Different bases: take logarithms of both sides and use the power law

blocks.prompt: 19 Solve the inequality \(3^{x + 1} < 7^{x}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Divide by the positive \(3^{x}\), take common logarithms (sign kept), and divide by \(\log\frac{7}{3}\), which is positive because \(\frac{7}{3} > 1\).

book_ref.quote: Being positive is not enough

steps: Base-10 log is strictly increasing: \(\log 3 < x\log\frac{7}{3}\)

blocks.prompt: 20 Solve the inequality \(\log_{\frac{2}{3}}(x^{2} - 5x + 4) \ge \log_{\frac{2}{3}}(x - 1)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find the domain of both logarithms; the base \(\frac{2}{3} < 1\) reverses the sign; intersect with the domain.

book_ref.quote: Keeping the inequality sign when the base is between 0 and 1

steps: Base \(\frac{2}{3}\) is between 0 and 1, so the sign is reversed: \(x^{2} - 5x + 4 \le x - 1\)
With the domain: \(4 < x \le 5\). Check \(x = 5\): arguments \(4\) and \(4\), equal logs; \(x = 4.5\): \(1.75 \le 3.5\)

blocks.prompt: 21 A bacteria culture grows as \(N = 400e^{kt}\) (\(t\) in hours) and reaches 1000 after 12 hours. Find (i) \(k\) (ii) \(N\) after 24 hours (iii) the time when \(N = 1600\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Substitute the known pair to find \(k\); make the exponential stand alone before taking \(\ln\).

book_ref.quote: Many natural and physical processes such as population growth and radioactive decay

blocks.prompt: 22 A radioactive substance decays as \(N = 900e^{-0.03t}\) (\(t\) in years). Find (i) the amount after 10 years (ii) the time when 300 remains (iii) its half-life. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: (i) is direct substitution; (ii) and (iii) have \(t\) in the exponent, so isolate \(e^{-0.03t}\) and take \(\ln\).

book_ref.quote: In growth, the quantity increases with time, while in decay it decreases with time.

blocks.prompt: 23 A machine produces a sound of level 70 dB (\(I_{0} = 10^{-12}\ \text{W/m}^{2}\)). (i) Find its intensity. (ii) A second machine is 100 times as intense. Find its sound level. (iii) What is the level of the threshold intensity? (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use \(L = 10\log\frac{I}{I_{0}}\): divide by 10 and change to exponential form to find \(I\); substitute to find \(L\).

book_ref.quote: makes logarithmic laws very useful in comparing sound levels in real-life situations

blocks.prompt: 24 Rs. 8000 is invested at 6% per annum for 2 years. Find the amount if interest is compounded (i) monthly (ii) continuously. (iii) At 7% compounded continuously, how long does a sum take to double? (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Discrete: \(A = P\left(1 + \frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}\) with \(n = 12\); continuous: \(A = Pe^{rt}\); for doubling, isolate \(e^{rt}\) and take \(\ln\).

book_ref.quote: Continuous compounding always gives slightly more than any discrete compounding at the same rate.
